title: ESM-Ezy mining identifies multicopper oxidases and asparaginases with experimentally improved catalytic properties
summary: The ESM-1b semantic-embedding mining strategy nominated low-sequence-similarity enzyme candidates. In the reported experimental assessment, 44% of tested multicopper oxidases outperformed their query enzymes in at least one measured property (including catalytic efficiency, heat/solvent tolerance or pH stability); 51% were reported to excel in environmental-remediation applications. Among mined L-asparaginases, 40% had higher specific activity and catalytic efficiency than query enzymes.
ai_technology: ESM-Ezy, using ESM-1b protein-language-model embeddings and semantic-space similarity

evidence.tested: In the reported experimental assessment, 44% of tested multicopper oxidases outperformed their query enzymes in at least one measured property (including catalytic efficiency, heat/solvent tolerance or pH stability); 51% were reported to excel in environmental-remediation applications.
evidence.unknown: Percentages describe the selected candidates and tested property comparisons in this study, not the fraction of all database enzymes that will be superior. The reported remediation suitability is assay-specific; environmental or industrial deployment is not established. Primary abstract/full-text search result checked; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: ESM-1b sequence embeddings and semantic-space similarity ranked low-similarity candidate enzymes from sequence databases for experimental follow-up; assays assessed catalytic properties of selected multicopper oxidases and L-asparaginases.
